key_insight: The best LLM judge matched physician-level agreement on this German clinical benchmark, but it still lacked the caution and abstention behavior clinicians showed.
clinical_relevance: Automated evaluation can help scale medical AI benchmarking, yet it should not be assumed to reproduce clinical judgment without explicit checks for safety and independence.
method: Built MedQADE, a standardized German open-response clinical benchmark with 3,800 items.
Annotated the set with 10 practicing physicians and 9 LLM evaluators.
Compared evaluator agreement, abstention behavior, and model-lineage bias.
evidence_signal: Gemini 3 Flash achieved near-physician agreement (κ=0.694 vs. κ=0.709), but confidence intervals were wide and frontier models never abstained.
watch_item: Statistical agreement alone may hide unsafe evaluator behavior, including zero-abstention scoring and lineage-dependent bias.
paper_title: Clinician-Level Agreement Without Clinical Caution: LLM Evaluator Limits in Medical AI Benchmarking
